## Rule

**rot180** of the fixed **3×3** one-hot content, embedded top-left of the `[1,10,30,30]` canvas.
`output = np.rot90(input_grid, 2)`. Every NG140 grid (train/test/arc-gen) is exactly 3×3.
Verified: `rot90(grid,2)==output` on 265/265 visible pairs; byte-equal vs LIVE on 200265/200265.

## Algorithm sketch

```python
out_grid = np.rot90(in_grid, 2)   # 3x3 -> 3x3, embedded at top-left of 30x30
```

## Cost analysis

**LIVE / PRIMARY (5):** single **RoiAlign** node, `rois` F32[1,4]=4 + `batch_indices` INT64[1]=1 → params 5, memory 0.
The reversed ROI `[3.25, 3.25, -31.75, -31.75]` (x2<x1, y2<y1) resamples `output[r,c] = input[2−r, 2−c]` inside the
3×3 and out-of-bounds→0 elsewhere, exactly reproducing rot180-of-the-top-left-3×3 on the zero-padded canvas.
Output is the graph output (`"output"`) so it is not billed → memory 0. **cost 5**, profile == static.

**Dominant charged term:** the `rois`/`batch_indices` payload (5 params). No intermediate is materialized.

### Floor proof — 5 is the structural floor (perfect-25 / ≤1 is infeasible)

Grader: `points = max(1, 25 − log(max(1, memory+params)))` → perfect-25 needs `memory+params ≤ 1`, i.e. an
attribute-only (0-payload) graph. `calculate_params` counts initializers **and Constant-node tensors**
(constant-folding on), so there is no free-payload trick.

1. **The transform is a positional sub-region reflection** — reverse index order within `[0:3,0:3]`, zeros
   elsewhere. Not identity (Identity → visible 0/265) and not a whole-canvas symmetry (whole-canvas
   Slice-reverse → visible 0/265; content moves to the opposite corner).
2. **No 0-payload op reflects.** Attribute-only spatial ops (Transpose, DepthToSpace, SpaceToDepth, Reshape,
   Identity, Flatten, Squeeze) either swap axes or do monotonic block reshuffles; none reverse index order
   within an axis. So a cost-0 perfect-25 graph is impossible.
3. **Every reflecting op carries ≥5 counted payload.** RoiAlign `rois[1,4]`+`batch_indices[1]`=5 (both inputs
   required); MaxRoiPool `rois[1,5]`=5; Slice-reverse(→[1,10,3,3])+Pad=≥16. The region-resample floor is 5.

**WALL at 5. Perfect-25 (≤1) is infeasible.** See `task140/hard_records/perfect25_ceiling_leq1.md`.

> Superseded floor proofs deleted per protocol: the old "210 floor" (V3 crop-collapse canvas) was retracted
> when the RoiAlign cost-5 route shipped; the old "byte-equal one-hot output forces a 90 B [1,10,3,3] BOOL
> emit" assumed a Pad-back structure — RoiAlign emits the output directly with zero billed memory.

## Don't-do log

_Record ruled-out hypotheses here so future agents don't retry them._

**2026-07-07 perfect-25 ceiling (cost ≤1) hunt (bo_ng_cld_worker3): WALL at 5 — do NOT retry.**
LIVE is a cost-5 RoiAlign (reversed ROI). rot180-of-3×3-top-left is a positional sub-region reflection:
Identity (cost 0) → visible 0/265; whole-canvas Slice-reverse (cost 8) → visible 0/265. No attribute-only
(0-payload) op reverses index order within an axis, and every reflecting op (RoiAlign/MaxRoiPool=5,
Slice+Pad=16) carries ≥5 counted params. Perfect-25 is infeasible. Full argument:
`task140/hard_records/perfect25_ceiling_leq1.md`. (Old sub-210 canvas-floor notes below are moot — the
RoiAlign route obsoleted the whole crop-collapse family.)

**2026-05-19 crop-to-active-grid (worker-7, Group S sweep): NOT VIABLE.**
All internal intermediates already operate at 3×3 or smaller (earliest Slice already crops).
The only [30,30] tensor is the model OUTPUT, which ORT does not bill in activation memory.
Prepending a Slice(input→[1,10,3,3]) adds a 360-byte intermediate without removing any,
increasing cost. Verified: task087 crop-test went 376→748. Do not retry crop on any Group S task.
(Superseded as the *headline* by the #8b channel-collapse below — the channel collapse, NOT a same-dtype
crop, is what removes the 360 B; the old note's "crop alone doesn't help" still holds.)

**2026-06-10 sub-210 hunt (worker-5, #8b): 210 is the floor — do NOT sub-floor-hunt. Measured rejections:**
- **Full-canvas Equal-as-output** (Pad color canvas → `[1,1,30,30]`, Equal = free output): **3739** — the
  padded `[1,1,30,30]` F32 (3600) dominates. The crossover law favors cropped-BOOL at this 3×3 grid.
- **QLinearConv** to emit a U8 canvas directly (skip the F32 conv canvas): **9180** — `QuantizeLinear(input)`
  materializes a full `[1,10,30,30]` U8 (9000) before the conv consumes it.
- **opset-10 attribute Pad** (to drop the 8 pads-input params): Pad(BOOL) does **not load at opset 10**
  (`score_network_v2 → None`); opset 11+ requires the pads input tensor. Stuck with +8 params for the Pad.
- **1×1 Conv collapse (10 params) then Slice-crop**: rejected — outputs `[1,1,30,30]` F32 = 3600 B before crop.
- **Slice-crop input first to `[1,10,3,3]` then collapse**: rejected — the `[1,10,3,3]` F32 crop = 360 B (= LIVE)
  dominates. The dilated crop-collapse Conv is the only way to avoid that 360.
The dominant 90 B (`onehot_b` Equal `[1,10,3,3]` BOOL) is the irreducible one-hot info content; see Floor proof.
